decisions.reason: Although Product A looks more niche and had a delayed rollout signal, it is still a visible investment in particle-therapy QA that management is likely to continue backing rather than reverse quickly.
Product B is a core dosimetry instrument in the firm's established competence area, so sunk development, calibration, and support commitments make withdrawal unlikely absent clear failure evidence.
Product C fits the firm's core ionization-chamber portfolio and prior public launch commitment, which under an escalation-of-commitment logic favors retaining it on the market.
As a standard clinical ionization chamber, Product D sits close to the firm's mainstream customer needs and installed-service model, making continuation the more likely choice.
Product E supports routine relative dosimetry workflows central to the firm's measurement business, so management would likely justify and continue the existing investment.
Product F is a classic thimble chamber within the firm's longstanding technical domain, and its portfolio fit and support obligations point toward keeping it available.
